claims.text: Standard metal rollers and guide plates are susceptible to corrosion by high-temperature liquid aluminum.
Applying a dense, adherent alumina-based ceramic coating to contact surfaces will significantly reduce liquid-aluminum-induced corrosion.
The relevant hot-dip aluminum plating exposure temperature is approximately 650–700°C.
The alumina ceramic coating forms a physical barrier between liquid aluminum and the underlying metal substrate.
Alumina has a high melting point relative to the proposed operating temperature.
Alumina is chemically inert toward liquid aluminum under the proposed operating conditions.
The alumina layer minimizes interfacial reactions between liquid aluminum and the metal substrate.
The alumina layer limits aluminum penetration into the metal substrate.
Reduced interfacial reaction and aluminum penetration reduce corrosion of the substrate.
Alumina-coated components will have lower corrosion rates than uncoated components under identical plating conditions.
Alumina-coated components will have longer service lives than uncoated components under identical plating conditions.
Poor coating adhesion or coating defects may diminish the protective effect.
Operating beyond the ceramic material's stability limits may diminish the protective effect.
